signals.title: NZD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5448 below all major moving averages, while CHF leads G10 performance. In the weekly G10 scorecard, CHF gained +0.514% across 6 pairs while NZD lost -0.580% across 4 pairs, creating a 1.094% bilateral spread. Fundamental support aligns with the Economic Surprise Index, where CHF shows strong positive momentum at +28.0 compared to NZD's strong negative read of -15.4. RBNZ policy rate at 2.75% versus SNB at 0.00% offers a +275bp nominal carry advantage to NZD, but the real policy rate differential (-1.02% CHF vs +0.39% NZD) and persistent data misses weigh on the Kiwi. Spot NZD/USD trades cheap vs BEER fair value model at z=-2.03σ, but macro momentum favors continued CHF outperformance. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/CHF, broad G10 divergence favors CHF strength against NZD. Catalyst: Switzerland Employment Level release on 24 Nov. Risk: RBNZ rate hike pricing expands following upcoming macro releases, narrowing the G10 performance spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Crowded Carry + Risk Reversal Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.35, holding above the SMA20/50/200 cluster at 158.69/158.04/158.88. The SOFR-TONA OIS carry differential of +269bp (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%) supports the pair's upside structure, but key technical boundaries require caution. Price at 159.35 remains below 160.00, the key level that has previously triggered BoJ verbal warnings, with intervention risk rising on a sustained break above 160.00. CFTC positioning shows JPY net short at -29,545 contracts sitting at the 85th percentile of its 52-week range (z=+1.12), indicating a crowded carry trade. Options pricing shows strong downside hedging demand with 25d Risk Reversals at -1.87 put skew alongside an elevated Vol Risk Premium (IV 7.7% vs HV30 5.5%, VRP +2.2%). Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY, carry support remains dominant while VIX stays contained. Catalyst: BoJ Trimmed Mean CPI release on 25 Nov. Risk: VIX clears 30 or BoJ/MoF conducts physical intervention, triggering a sharp short-covering unwind.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Rate Differential + Technical Downtrend
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.0908, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.1102/1.1221/1.1500 in a confirmed downtrend structure. The Fed policy rate of 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% creates a +135bp spread favoring USD (+148bp on SOFR vs €STR OIS basis), structurally capping EUR/USD upside. Leveraged Funds net positioning sits at -105,891 contracts, placing EUR at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range (z=-1.68) following a weekly shift of -7,287 contracts. Options volatility reflects moderate hedging demand with 1M ATM IV at 6.2% vs HV30 at 5.1% (VRP +1.1%), while 25d Risk Reversals show a mild put skew of -0.44. BEER fair value model indicates spot is stretched cheap at z=-3.20σ (model fair value 1.1093), suggesting mean-reversion potential once rates momentum stabilizes. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, carry advantage and technical breakdown favor dollar dominance. Catalyst: Germany GDP data release on 25 Nov. Risk: German GDP prints well above 0.2% forecast, prompting hawkish ECB repricing and short-covering.
